chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who said: He narrated to me Abu Abdullah al-Razi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Uthman, from his father, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
There are four characteristics which do not belong to a believer: he is not insane; he doesn’t go around begging at the people’s doors; he is not born of adultery and he is not gay.

key_terms.يَنْكَحُ فِي دُبُرِهِ: he marries in his rear (anal intercourse)

ai.seo_question: What are the four characteristics that are not found in a believer according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents these four traits as definitive exclusions from the state of *i'timad* (being relied upon as a trustworthy believer), linking physical and social integrity to spiritual status. While 'insanity' and 'born of adultery' denote inherent or lineage-based impurities, the latter two—begging and anal intercourse—highlight specific social and sexual moralities valued in Shia jurisprudence. This classification underscores the holistic nature of faith, where external behavior and internal purity are inextricably linked.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-68 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Abu Abdullah al-Razi, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Abi Uthman, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abi Basir, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), “
There are four characteristics which do not belong to a believer: he is not insane; he doesn’t go around begging at the people’s doors; he is not born of adultery and he is not gay.”
